source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Small to large tree, usually smaller westward, often coarse and densely branched toward base
morphology_documented.leaves: Narrow at base, wedge- to club-shaped overall, nearly entire to three shallow apical lobes, rarely basal lateral lobes
morphology_documented.habitat: Chiefly upland on sandy, occasionally gravelly or silty soils

regional_flora_key_traits.fruit: Second-autumn acorn maturity (red/black oak group-level key)

source_scope_note: Species, genus-key and secondary-source material separated; blank traits are not inferred from existing site data.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: The source's generic red-oak-group bristle tips and second-season acorns are group-level traits, not species description
preservation: Additive research record only; originals, prior morphology, photos, source credits, galleries unchanged
